title: I am he (John 18:1–11)
hook: the soldiers fall back at his words

segments.voice: Yesterday, the prayer that closed the supper: that they all may be one. That was your line too. What kind word did you say about another church? Day five hundred twenty-six.

Picture a garden at night across a small valley from the city walls. Olive trees, the smell of crushed leaves, and down the slope a line of lights coming up: torches and lanterns, a detachment of soldiers, officers from the chief priests, the glint of weapons. And leading them, someone who knows exactly where to find this garden, because he's been here many times. It's Judas. Most people expect the next part to be a chase in the dark. John tells it very differently.
screen: `A GARDEN ACROSS THE KIDRON.` → `TORCHES COMING UP THE SLOPE.` → `JUDAS KNOWS THE PLACE.`

segments.voice: John says Jesus knew all that was coming upon him, and he went forth. He doesn't wait to be found. He walks out to meet them and asks, whom seek ye? Jesus of Nazareth, they say. And he answers with two words, in Greek egō eimi, which the Douay-Rheims renders: "I am he." Then John adds this: "As soon therefore as he had said to them: I am he; they went backward, and fell to the ground." Armed men, with torches, fall over. Why? John doesn't explain it. But the reader has been hearing egō eimi all through this Gospel: I am the bread of life, I am the light of the world, and once, startlingly, before Abraham was made, I am. In the scriptures, I am is how God names himself to Moses at the burning bush. So when Jesus says it in the garden, John lets the words land with weight, and the arresting party ends up on the ground. Jesus asks again, whom seek ye? Same answer, same reply. Then: if you seek me, let these go their way. He trades himself for his friends, the good shepherd in a single sentence. Peter, of course, draws a sword and cuts off the right ear of the high priest's servant, and only John gives us his name: Malchus. Jesus stops him: put up thy sword into the scabbard. He isn't trapped here. He's choosing. And it all begins with saying, plainly, who he is.
screen: `HE GOES OUT TO MEET THEM.` · `EGŌ EIMI: I AM HE.` · `THEY FALL TO THE GROUND.` · `LET THESE GO THEIR WAY.` · then, large: `I AM HE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: stand by your name. If you can, stand up. Feet flat, shoulders easy, head level. Breathe. Say your own name once, quietly, not as a question. Then think of one place where you tend to hide who you are, or what you believe, or what you did: a meeting, a family dinner, a conversation you dodge. Picture yourself there, simply answering, that's me. If you pray, you can hold Jesus's words, I am he, and ask for courage. If you don't, just stand and breathe. The bell holds the time.
I am he. Jesus's answer to the soldiers in the garden, egō eimi, and they fall back to the ground. Today's word.
Your line: I am he. Today, when someone asks who did it or who's responsible, and it was you, say so first. Day five hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Catholics hear John's whole Passion, including the arrest in the garden, read aloud at the Celebration of the Lord's Passion on Good Friday, often with several readers taking the parts.

original.note: Greek: I am (John 18:5), the same words as the great I am sayings.

trapdoor: what you thought: Jesus confirming his identity, like showing an ID.
what it means: he steps forward, names himself, and protects his friends; the arrest happens on his terms.
what a scholar hears: egō eimi echoes John 8:58 and God's self-naming in Exodus 3:14 (Greek Septuagint: egō eimi ho ōn); only John names Malchus.

notes: 'Put up thy sword into the scabbard' and 'let these go their way' given without quotation marks; close to Douay wording.
John doesn't name the garden Gethsemane; the hook says 'a garden across a small valley' (the Kidron). Confirm.
The arresting party: a cohort (speira) plus temple officers. Described loosely. Confirm.
Exodus 3:14 LXX 'egō eimi ho ōn'. Confirm.
